reason: The cited evidence shows that laser cladding of WC-reinforced AlCoCrFeNi HEA improves hardness and wear resistance on steel, but provides no data or discussion for Ti6Al4V substrates. The key premise that this specific coating system will bond well, avoid detrimental interfacial reactions, and produce the claimed improvements on titanium alloy is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Laser cladding can produce a metallurgically bonded, hard, wear-resistant AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating on a metallic substrate
Adding WC particles to an AlCoCrFeNi HEA matrix increases hardness and wear resistance
The combination of laser cladding, AlCoCrFeNi HEA, and WC reinforcement is effective on a steel substrate
The proposed mechanism (WC hard particle reinforcement, HEA solid solution/dispersion strengthening, fine microstructure from rapid solidification) is valid for Ti6Al4V
